conviction_note: The print turns on the first FY27 guide. Public evidence points both ways: bid-season prices up about double digits, a competitor's Lake Erie mine flooded, and a possible capital-allocation update, against lower committed volumes, an El Nino winter forecast, Goderich costs and governance turnover. The findings net to about -0.3, so p_up stays at 50 and the scaled number is 0. abs_move stays large (12%) because a full-year guide initiation has moved this name 13.8% (Dec 2025) and the median reaction is 13.8%.
bar: Q4 FY26: consensus EPS about -$0.01 and revenue about $221.1M (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-15, https://finviz.com/news/422870/compass-minerals-heads-into-fiscal-year-end-needing-proof-that-salt-pricing-can-outrun-goderich-costs). The company's own FY26 guide (8-K 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227654/000122765426000050/cmp-q32026earningsreleasee.htm) implies Q4 revenue of about $200-246M (midpoint ~$223M), total adj. EBITDA $26-50M (FY $218-242M, midpoint $230M, 9M actual $191.6M) and salt adj. EBITDA $36-47M (FY floor $225M). The Q4 bar is therefore sourced to the company guide. The bar that matters, a FY27 adj. EBITDA consensus, is unsourced: one aggregator shows about $252M at an unclear, probably mid-2026, date. Every guide-dependent finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.68M shares with 4.0-4.2 days to cover (massive.com, settlement 2026-09-30; shortsqueeze.com, 2026-10-22), or 2.1M and 4.9% of float with 5.3 days on another source (equibles). That is moderate, not crowded. 25-delta skew is unusable (the baseline rejected -60.68 vol points). Put/call OI is 0.46 on only 1,106 contracts. The ATM spread is 45% of mid, so the 10.46% event-implied move is indicative only. Tape: -7.78% over 5 days and -10.0% over 20; the stock fell from $23.05 (Nov 12) to $19.27 (Nov 20) on rising volume (1.13M on Nov 20, about 2.7x the 20-day average, which was also monthly opex) with no news found; spot is $20.02, 40% off the 52-week high. Sentiment described as modestly bearish (EW preview 2026-11-15).

findings.finding: Management said on the Q3 call (2026-08-06) that 2026-27 highway bid-season pricing is 'kind of around double digits' overall, with 'substantial year-over-year price improvement', and that it would give 'tighter guidance' at this Q4 print. Public tenders since then show 10-15% (Vermont state contract, Cargill and Eastern Salt as winners) up to 60%+ in some Midwest and Mid-Atlantic municipal tenders (Crux Investor, 2026-11-05). So realised FY27 highway price could sit at or above the ~10% the company quoted (Q3 highway price was $83.74/ton vs $77.63).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last FY guide initiation (2025-12-08: FY26 adj. EBITDA guided at $200-240M alongside an EPS and revenue beat) drew a -13.81% reaction, so this name has sold guide initiations. The Q2 print, when bid-season price commentary first appeared, drew +6.73% (2026-05-06).
findings.why_not_priced: The ~10% figure is public, but the stock has fallen about 20% since the Q3 print and sits near its post-earnings low ($20.57). That is not what a market crediting a double-digit price reset on ~8Mt of highway volume would look like. The tender evidence of increases well above 10% in several jurisdictions sits in municipal bid tabs and one secondary article, not in a company number. If it were priced, the stock would have held up into the guide rather than making new lows.
findings.independence: Vermont: https://www.vlct.org/node/4521 (10-15% above 2025-26). Crux Investor, 2026-11-05: https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/road-salt-bids-rise-over-60-why-the-market-still-needs-new-mines (60%+, secondary). DuPage County renewed with Compass at +5% (Downers Grove agenda, https://agendadocs.downers.us/public/docs/agendas/2026/08_04_2026/MOT_2026-11295.pdf), which cuts against the high end. The FY27 bar is unsourced, so this finding is capped.

findings.finding: Management said it 'expect[s] to commit to a reduced volume profile for fiscal 2027 relative to the past seasons', on 'an assumption of more normalized winter weather'. Since then the forecast has turned against even normal weather: Drought.gov's Great Lakes ENSO brief (Nov 2026) gives a 100% chance of El Nino through early 2027 and 83% that it is the strongest on record. NOAA CPC (Nov 19 update) favours above-normal temperatures across the northern US and Great Lakes, and NWS Gaylord favours below-normal snowfall. FY27 volume and the first quarter (Oct-Dec) carry downside to a guide built on normal weather.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume and weather-driven guide moves have been sold: the FY26 guide initiation (2025-12-08) drew -13.81%, and Q3 (2026-08-05), where salt volume and cost disappointed, drew -14.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: The reduced committed volumes are public (August call) and the El Nino forecast is widely reported, so most of this is likely in the 17% slide since Nov 12. The unpriced part is how management handles it: a guide that assumes normal weather despite a record El Nino forecast would be haircut by the Street on the call. That gap is visible only once the range is published.
findings.independence: Company statement on the Q3 call: https://www.webull.com/news/15717640508556288. NWS Gaylord outlook: https://www.weather.gov/media/apx/WinterOutlook.pdf. The weather-to-company link is a proxy; the company has not confirmed any weather impact on Q1 FY27.

findings.finding: Competitor Morton Salt halted underground operations at its Fairport Harbor, Ohio mine (about 1-1.5 Mt/yr under Lake Erie) after a water inflow on 2026-10-22, laid off 77 workers, and had found neither the source nor a restart date by mid-November. Deliveries to six Northeast Ohio counties are in doubt. This happened after Compass last spoke (Aug 5) and removes capacity from Compass's core Great Lakes market (its Cleveland mine is in the same region) during a season management already called tight on inventory. Compass can win spot or emergency tonnage at high prices, and management can cite it as FY27 upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior Compass print on a competitor outage. The stock rose from $21.00 (Oct 22) to $23.31 (Oct 30) in the week the outage was reported, then gave all of it back by Nov 20.
findings.why_not_priced: No sell-side estimate has changed since the event, as far as found. The price round-tripped: the post-outage gain is fully gone at $20.02, below the pre-outage $21.00. If the market credited Compass with incremental tonnage or pricing, the stock would not be below where it traded before a competitor lost 1-1.5 Mt of capacity. Compass has not said whether it is supplying affected customers, so the transmission is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: News5 Cleveland on the layoffs: https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/morton-salt-to-lay-off-77-workers-after-water-breach-at-fairport-harbor-mine. Spectrum News, 2026-11-09, on county responses (ODOT has 655k tons on hand, 76% of storage, which tempers the shortage): https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/columbus/news/2026/11/09/ohio-counties-respond-to-salt-mine-closure. The Crux 2026-11-05 article shares the pricing context with the first finding.

findings.finding: Salt costs are the line the stock sold on last time. In Q3, salt operating income fell 25% to $21.2M and salt adj. EBITDA 15% on Goderich hoisting below planned cost, extra maintenance at both US mines, higher headcount and freight; the CEO said costs 'have not come down the way we expected', and the COO was replaced (2026-08-03). The FY26 salt EBITDA guide was cut to $225-236M, which leaves Q4 salt EBITDA of $36-47M (9M actual $189.3M). A Q4 below the $225M full-year floor, or a FY27 guide without visible per-ton cost relief, repeats the Q3 pattern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-05), on salt cost and margin disappointment: -14.55%. Q1 FY26 (2026-02-04): -14.77%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock fell 14.55% on it and has slid further. What is not priced is whether Q4 lands inside the guide. The implied salt EBITDA range is wide ($36-47M) and the Q4 consensus revenue ($221M) sits at the guide midpoint, so a low-end salt result is not in the bar. The preview names a result below $225M as the credibility test.
findings.independence: The Q3 call transcript carries the same cost statements: https://www.webull.com/news/15717640508556288. The EW preview, 2026-11-15, frames Goderich cost as the print's swing factor: https://finviz.com/news/422870/compass-minerals-heads-into-fiscal-year-end-needing-proof-that-salt-pricing-can-outrun-goderich-costs. Both rest on the same company disclosures.

findings.finding: A 50% Section 338 tariff applied to Canadian goods, including Goderich salt shipped to the US, from 2026-08-19 until salt was excluded effective 2026-09-15. The company announced the exclusion on 2026-09-10 and disclosed no cost or refund. That leaves about four weeks of the fiscal Q4 summer-fill shipping window exposed; the company said commercial agreements would minimise it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a tariff cost.
findings.why_not_priced: The cost was never quantified, and the exclusion headline let the market treat the issue as closed. A one-off cost in a seasonally small quarter, with no path to the FY27 guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Sen. Moran on the tariff's effect, 2026-08-19: https://kspress.com/news/2026/08/19/us-sen-jerry-moran-warns-of-canadian-salt-tariffs%E2%80%99-effect-on-kansas-taxpayers

findings.finding: Plant Nutrition has beaten its own targets four quarters running. The FY26 segment EBITDA guide was raised to $49-57M from $43-47M (above the $40-50M 'restore' target, even after the Wynyard sale). Q3 segment EBITDA was up 32% to $15.0M, and per-unit costs fell. The guide leaves Q4 segment EBITDA of $4-12M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 Plant Nutrition beat came alongside a -14.55% reaction driven by salt: the segment does not carry the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: it falls inside a raised company guide, and the segment is about 15-20% of revenue. Net of the rest of the company, it only moves the stock if salt holds.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the salt-cost finding. EW preview: https://finviz.com/news/422870/compass-minerals-heads-into-fiscal-year-end-needing-proof-that-salt-pricing-can-outrun-goderich-costs

findings.finding: Net leverage fell to 2.8x from 4.3x, the remaining $150M of 2027 notes was redeemed, and S&P upgraded the rating to B+. The Earnings Whispers preview says management promised a capital allocation update at this report after a Board discussion. The dividend has been suspended, so any reinstatement or buyback would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return announcement in the last seven prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The promise comes from an AI-assisted preview; no primary transcript quote was found. Management also said debt reduction 'where it makes sense' remains a priority, so the update may be debt-first. A stock near its low with no yield support suggests no capital return is expected.
findings.independence: Leverage figures from the 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227654/000122765426000050/cmp-q32026earningsreleasee.htm. A Fintool AI summary of the Q1 call mentions board capital-allocation conversations (secondary, not a primary quote).

findings.finding: Chief Accounting Officer Ashley Ward resigned on 2026-10-22, effective the next day, one month before the fiscal-year-end 10-K. The 8-K states the resignation was 'not the result of any disagreement'. She was replaced on 2026-10-28 by Brett Teuscher, the Senior Director of Internal Audit, who joined in May 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. Compass has a history of restatement and filing delays (an earlier 'delayed' Q4 drew a BMO target cut), which is why an accounting-officer exit before a 10-K is worth filing.
findings.why_not_priced: A quiet 8-K Item 5.02 with no press coverage found. It matters only if the 10-K or the release carries a control or timing issue. The 'no disagreement' language argues against it, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Director David Safran, the former CEO of Kissner Group (a rock-salt competitor) who was added to the board in December 2025, resigned on 2026-10-09 after about ten months. The board shrank from nine to eight members, and no reason was given.
findings.why_not_priced: An 8-K with no press release. A salt-industry director leaving a salt company within a year is odd, but it carries no number.
findings.independence: The December 2025 appointment release: https://businesswire.com/news/home/20251218311390/en/Compass-Minerals-Announces-Additions-to-Board-of-Directors. Governance turnover alongside the CAO exit, but a separate document.

findings.finding: The stock fell 16.4% from $23.05 (Nov 12) to $19.27 (Nov 20) into the print on rising volume (1.13M shares on Nov 20 against a 414k 20-day average), with no company news found. That leaves it below the post-Q3 low and the pre-Morton-outage level, and lowers the bar for the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of seven prior prints fell. The two up moves (+26.21% in May 2025, +6.73% in May 2026) are not linked in the baseline to pre-print run-ups.
findings.why_not_priced: Sized at 0 because the drawdown has no identified cause, and an unexplained drawdown is not evidence of over-reaction. Filed so the panel sees the tape. Nov 20 was monthly options expiry, which may explain the volume.

outside_window.finding: The record-strength El Nino winter's actual snowfall over Dec 2026 to Mar 2027, and the duration of Morton's Fairport outage, decide FY27 volumes and spot sales. Both are observable only after the exit window, beyond what the guide states.

searched_and_found_nothing: No Compass news, analyst action or 8-K found for Nov 13-20, 2026, which would explain the pre-print slide
No sourced FY27 adj. EBITDA consensus beyond one undated aggregator figure (~$252M)
Earnings call transcript on Benzinga returned 403; used the Webull copy instead

baseline_tension: The skew is unusable and the option-implied move indicative only (45% spread). The -10% 20-day run-up and bearish sentiment already price the cost and volume negatives, while the positives (competitor outage, pricing) were given back in the slide. Neither side has a company-level number the market has not seen, so the evidence offsets and p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the FY27 bar is unsourced (one undated aggregator), so the guide-dependent findings were capped. Pricing went +1.5 to +1.0, Morton outage +1.5 to +1.0, El Nino/volume -1.0 to -0.8.
Rule 5 (unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the pre-print slide (positioning) went +1.0 to 0.0, kept filed for the panel.
Rule 6 (inside guide): Plant Nutrition sits inside a raised company guide, so it went +0.3 to +0.1.
Rule 2 (one-off): the Section 338 tariff cost has no path to the guide, so it went -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 5 (documents beat inference): the capital-allocation update rests on an AI-assisted preview, so it went +0.8 to +0.5.
Rules 1 and 3: this name sold its last guide initiation despite a beat (-13.8%). That keeps p_up at 50 and abs_move at 12, unchanged from the draft.
Goderich salt cost went -1.5 to -1.2, because its own why_not_priced says it is mostly priced. CAO exit went -0.5 to -0.4. Safran unchanged.
